claims.text: The review's challenge table holds five questions: database per shop (ADR 0013), protection while a large shop waits (ADR 0016, from release 2), report across shops (open), contract demanding its own copy (ADR 0012 review condition), shop shrinking after a move (open).
The design review states it does not reopen ADRs 0012, 0013, 0016 and multi-shop-data-rollout.md.
ADR 0013: with 1,000 shops, a schema or database per shop turns each release of a service into 1,000 migration runs and each new shop into creating a schema or database; shared tables keep one run.
ADR 0016: each shop has a ceiling, a fixed share of concurrent reads per process (assumed a quarter of 20); the ceiling is not a reserved place.

ADR 0016: the limit needs the request's shop from the access token, from release 2 of multi-shop-data-rollout.md (a plan adding shop_id in three releases; release 2: token carries the caller's shop); Program.cs keeps orders and catalog-reads unchanged at stage-4.

claims.text: ADR 0016 review condition: a shop that often needs more than its share moves to option three (own database or deployment) under ADR 0013's review condition.
catalog-reads counts every caller of one process together: 20 places and 5 queue places, so before release 2 nothing stops a busy shop from using them all.
At the time of the review, the report across all shops (one shop in its own database) is open, no ADR decides it; owners: product owner with a backend developer; the report design needs its own ADR.
In PostgreSQL 17 one query cannot name a table in another database; it is refused with "cross-database references are not implemented".
ADR 0012 first review condition: a shop whose contract demands its own copy of the system gets a separate copy of the same system; other shops are served as before.
ADR 0012 comments received: the product owner asked whether a large shop could have its own copy from the start; answer: no, until a contract demands it.
Open in the review: a moved shop that shrinks has no condition for moving back; owner: team lead; next step: add a review condition at the first such case.
ADR 0013 decided with an assumed 1,000 shops; ADR 0013 also weighed a schema per shop, rejected because each schema change runs once per schema and opening a shop means creating a schema.

Answer a challenge from the accepted ADR's reason when the facts it weighed still hold; argue again, through a new ADR, when a challenge shows a driver has changed (e.g. tens of shops instead of 1,000).
A gap found in review is recorded as an open question with an owner rather than fixed in the session, unless the gap breaks one of the design's own drivers.
ADRs 0012, 0013 and 0016 each list options ('Các phương án'), a comment deadline ('Hạn góp ý') and comments received ('Ý kiến đã nhận').
